notes:
CHR-618/CHR-621: replaces the old fixed 4-column grid at tile scale 0.8. Canonical Board state, covering ticket states 1–4 together on one screen (toolbar, pin affordance including its unpinned state, pinned-vs-match distinction, clear pins):

- Sidebar filter is "dialog", matching `open-project-dialog`, `init-project-dialog`, `no-project-empty-state` (3 matches). `open-project-dialog` is pinned (filled `$pin-button`); the other two sidebar rows show the unpinned `default` pin-button variant, so both pin states are visible in the sidebar list, not just the board.
- `app-shell` is pinned but does not match "dialog" — it still appears on the board because the board shows filter matches ∪ pinned screens (see the design-system decision `chr621-filter-lives-in-sidebar` for why the filter input itself lives only in the sidebar, not duplicated in the toolbar).
- Board tiles: `init-project-dialog` and `no-project-empty-state` are matches only — solid border, unpinned pin-button, demonstrating state 2's unpinned affordance on tiles too. `open-project-dialog` matches and is pinned — solid border, filled pin-button. `app-shell` is pinned-only — dashed accent border plus a `$tag-chip` `badge` reading "pinned · outside filter", the state-3 distinguishing marker.
- `$board-toolbar`'s `status` slot reports "4 shown — 3 matches · 2 pinned"; its `actions` slot holds a `$btn` "Clear pins" (ticket state 4) — shown here because pins are non-empty; `board-view-empty` shows the toolbar without it since there is nothing to clear.
- The filter hint under the search field is trimmed to the match count only ("3 matches") — the longer explanation of filter ∪ pins sharing lives here in the screen notes and in the `chr621` tag notes, not as on-canvas copy (CTO review feedback: that text read as documentation, not UI).
- The dashed SVG line between `open-project-dialog` and `app-shell` reflects the real `app-shell → open-project-dialog` flow edge that exists on `app-shell` (its `si-open` row); Edges are on (default toolbar variant).
- Sidebar rows and board tiles carry `data-flow-target` to their screens, consistent with `app-shell`'s existing screen-list pattern — clicking a tile opens that screen, same as clicking its sidebar row.

See also: `board-view-empty` (filter matches nothing, no pins), `board-view-presented` (agent-set-view indicator), `board-view-zoomed-out` (fit-all, edges off, many tiles), `board-view-zoomed-in` (200%, one tile) — the remaining states from the CHR-621 ticket.
